Hi Fang,

It looks like you will need to write some user-defined distributions. Please see Section 12.2 of the NIMBLE manual and this example from our website.

For the improper density proportional to 1/x, it's fine to write the improper "density" function as the "d" function for NIMBLE, though it won't make sense to write a random generation "r" function; you can just let NIMBLE define a dummy placeholder "r" function.

For the density for 'y', you'll need to use the 'pnorm' function, which is available for writing nimbleFunction run code. Again, you can just let NIMBLE define a dummy placeholder "r" function.

-chris
